title: An Image Is a Buffer With Opinions: Stride, Channels and Saturation

questions.question: A camera gives you a frame 13 pixels wide. What is the distance from the start of one row to the start of the next?
options: Usually 16, because rows are padded so each begins at an address the hardware likes
13, the width
13 times the bytes per pixel, always
Whatever you allocate it to be
questions.explanation: Every capture library reports it: bytesPerLine, linesize, step, rowPitch. It can change between frames when a format or resolution changes.

questions.question: A vertical line at column 10 is read from that frame using the width in place of the stride. What comes back?
options: A diagonal: the line walks three columns left per row, with seven of eight rows wrong and the first one right
The line, shifted three columns left on every row
Nothing, since the indices go out of range
The line, correct, since the padding is at the end
questions.explanation: The first row being right is the whole difficulty. A test on one row passes, and so does a test on a frame whose width happens to be a multiple of four.

questions.question: The bytes 32, 64, 200, 255 are read once as B,G,R,A and once as R,G,B,A. What is the difference?
options: A mostly red pixel and a mostly blue one, with nothing reporting an error because all four bytes were valid either way
The alpha channel is wrong in one of them
One of them is out of range
They differ only in the green channel
questions.explanation: Green and alpha sit in the same place in both, and so does grey. A test on a grey card or a white balance check passes under both conventions, which is how it survives to the field.

questions.question: Every pixel of an image has 100 added to it with a plain cast back to uint8_t. What happens to a pixel of 200?
options: It becomes 44: the brightest parts of the picture come out black, which looks like a sensor fault
It becomes 255, clamped
It becomes 300, stored in the next byte
It is undefined behaviour and the sanitizer catches it
questions.explanation: Conversion to an unsigned type is defined to wrap, so no sanitizer will say anything. Everything up to 155 is fine, which is most of a normal picture.

questions.question: What is the general rule that covers brightness, frame differences, blurs and gains?
options: The pixel is the storage, not the arithmetic: compute in int or float, decide what to do with anything out of range, and cast once on the way back
Always use saturating arithmetic on pixels
Always use floating point for images
Clamp the input rather than the output
questions.explanation: Nine pixels of 200 in a blur add to 1800, which is seven times what fits, and a - b on unsigned pixels is enormous wherever b is larger.

questions.question: What should a test image contain to find all three of this lesson's faults?
options: A width that needs padding, a pixel that is clearly red, and values at 0, 1, 254 and 255
A representative photograph at the camera's native resolution
A grey card at several exposures
The largest frame the camera can produce
questions.explanation: 640 by 480 hides the stride, a grey pixel hides the channel order, and a mid-grey image hides the saturation. Each fault needs one specific property in the picture.
